source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: In the hall, by the desk, a nurse sorted through files. A sudden cry from a distant bay caused her to glance up, her eyes scanning the room where patients lay on gurneys, monitors beeping and IV drips steady. She moved swiftly, checking charts, her steps quickened by the urgency of the scene. Behind the curtain, a doctor tended to a man in distress, his friend pacing beside him, muttering under his breath about the endless wait. The triage desk buzzed with activity, the receptionist calling out names, distributing colored wristbands, and sorting through forms, her hands never still. Around her, the emergency room was a hive of motion, nurses and doctors darting between patients, each step measured by the gravity of their task. Two hours had passed, yet the man's condition worsened, his companion growing more anxious, his complaints louder. The intercom crackled, paging specialists, adding to the chaos. In the midst of it all, a woman collapsed, her friend shouting for help, drawing attention to a new crisis. The doctor rushed over, his face a mask of determination, ready to face whatever came next.

In the heart of the bustling hospital, through the swinging doors, a nurse weaved between the crowded chairs and gurneys lining the corridor. Each patient, with their own stories of pain and worry, awaited their turn as the medical staff rushed past, checking monitors and adjusting drips behind the drawn curtains. A man in the corner clutched his chest, his eyes wide with fear, while his companion fidgeted anxiously, muttering under her breath about the endless wait.
